newsitem.title: USA: Texan who battered 22 emus to death escapes charge.
newsitem.headline: Texan who battered 22 emus to death escapes charge.

text.p: A Texas emu breeder who clubbed 22 of his birds to death with a baseball bat will escape criminal charges because his actions were not illegal under state law, prosecutors said on Thursday.
Stephen Vinson, a physician, used an aluminium bat to batter the flightless birds to death at his ranch in Colleyville, near Fort Worth, last month.
He had tried to herd them to another site but was having difficulty and, frustrated by his financial losses in breeding the once-valuable birds, began killing them.

Vinson faced possible cruelty charges but Richard Alpert, a prosecutor with the Tarrant County district attorney's office, said on Thursday that Texas law allowed owners to kill their own animals as long as they did not torture them.

"His intent was to kill the birds, not torture them. I certainly don't like the way he did it but he didn't cross that line," Alpert said in a telephone interview. "I just don't have a law I can use against him to prosecute him."
Animal rights activists were outraged by the decision not to prosecute.

"What he did was definitely against the law. Killing these birds humanely for meat is one thing but beating them to death is certainly not the way to go," said Reed Young, a cruelty investigator for the Humane Society of North Texas.
Police found another 86 emus at Vinson's Colleyville ranch. A municipal judge gave custody of the birds to the humane society and they will be moved to a ranch in California this week.
The market for emu meat, oil and eggs boomed several years ago but quickly became saturated as large numbers of people started buying them and breeding them in the hope of getting rich quick.
A pair of emus once fetched up to $40,000 but are now worth $400 or less, and owners have been unable to get rid of the birds. Even slaughterhouses are turning them away.
